name: Widget tap landing (attribution + forced refresh)
hostSurface: iOS DeepLinkRouter (which today reads only deliveryId/kind and discards every other query param) + TodayTabRoot; Android DeepLinkRouter + RootTabScreen + TodayTabViewModel.
purpose: Make the tap honest: open the exact surface the widget summarises, refresh it so the snapshot is rewritten, and record that this open came from the widget.
contents: Parse ?src=widget; force refresh() (not the idempotent load()); write the snapshot on success; post session_open {trigger:'widget'} — which requires the first funnel-event client either native app has ever had. Adds an 'Updated just now' / 'Updated Nm ago' line to the Today header so a user who tapped 'Open to refresh' can see it happened.
states: refreshing in place (content stays; never the skeleton)
cold start (full skeleton is acceptable — no prior content)
entryPoints: Any tap on either widget size
visualization: Refresh-in-place: a thin progress line under the header, content untouched. Blanking a screen someone tapped a widget to reach is the one thing this landing must never do.
uxNote: Two confirmed bugs, not risks. (1) Android maps 'today' to the hub BRIEFING screen, so a widget tap lands on a different payload than the widget showed — and for a T1 user that screen has no empty state and hard-errors. (2) Both Today view models are idempotent once loaded, so 'Open to refresh' can open a warm app, write no snapshot, and leave the widget grey permanently. Fix both here or F7 is a decoration.
